analysis: Examined head lines 1-1043 of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift. Changed lines visible here: L207 guard switches from autopilotAllowsModel to autopilotServesModel (load admission gate; semantics of the new predicate are defined elsewhere and not supplied; whether it is stricter or looser cannot be verified). L397 and L434 add transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) before load, and begin(.modelLoading, subject: modelId). Neither has a visible matching end/finish in this unit. The handle's lifecycle and its effect on transition-gated paths (challenge handling, attestation, T-053-style invalidation) live outside the supplied source. Base L1311 and head L1166-1168 and L1316-1324 are outside the visible units. Head L1166-1168 adds reconcileAutopilotPlacements() after slot removal in unload. This tightens behavior and blocks reloading an adopted model during the unload awaits. Unchanged security-relevant logic remains intact: weight-hash bracketing for reusable SSD cache (T-041 verified weightHash binding) at L548-L661, fail-closed on hash mismatch at L174-181, and markWeightHashUnavailable when hashes are unavailable. No regression was identified in the cache identity or the attestation hash publication paths (T-012, T-027). Integration questions: (1) Does autopilotServesModel admit any model that autopilotAllowsModel previously refused? (2) Is transitionGenerations.begin balanced on every early-throw path? Examples are the slot-cap throws at L411-427 and the throws before modelsLoading.insert. An unbalanced begin could cause availability or staleness issues, but is not a confidentiality issue. (3) Does the hidden head L1316-1324 change alter unload or retirement ordering?
